proposal.question: Go for the Bender egress-allowlist pilot? It restricts only traffic from Bender's CI workload bridge (fpcibender) to the office LAN, allowing just the Sulley git mirror, Hulk's Docker and npm caches, bridge DNS and DHCP; public internet stays open. It runs once Bender is naturally idle and fenced, with a one-command revert ready.
proposal.rationale: Today a CI workload VM on Bender can reach any office-network address. The pilot limits it to the three private services real jobs use (git mirror 192.168.1.214:8443, Docker cache 192.168.1.158:15000, npm cache 192.168.1.158:14873) plus DNS/DHCP, and rejects other private ranges; public internet access is unchanged. It is a single host, applied only when Bender is idle and drained, proven with a disposable VM and then natural jobs, and undone with one command (sudo -n /usr/local/lib/fp-ci/workload-lan.sh revert). The code paths it relies on are unchanged since Nov 2; live host state is rechecked at execution. Risk if wrong: a missed private dependency breaks checkout, installs or guest boot on Bender until reverted.

actions.label: Go: pilot on Bender
actions.instruction: Schedule the Bender egress-allowlist pilot per data/bender-egress-pilot-decision/report.md: apply only when Bender is naturally idle and fenced, keep the one-command revert ready, prove with disposable-VM probes and then natural jobs, no wider rollout without proof.

actions.label: No-go: keep open access
actions.instruction: Do not run the pilot; keep today's open office-network access for CI workloads.
